text:
samir: Morning folks — I accepted the org invite but GitHub still shows 'You need two-factor authentication' and I don't see the 'model-serving' repo in the org. I turned on 2FA earlier. Anyone know who to ping?

marta: Hey Samir — welcome! Quick checks: is the 2FA enabled on the same GitHub account you used for the invite? Also try logging out and back in after enabling. What's the exact error string?

samir: Error is 'You must enable two-factor authentication to access redwood-inference'. I enabled TOTP in Settings -> Security and it says 2FA is active.

charles: I can take a look. If you have the GitHub CLI, run `gh api /user/memberships/orgs/redwood-inference --jq .state` — if it says "pending" we need to resend.

samir: Ran it — output: "pending"

charles: I'll cancel and resend the invite. After I resend, accept it while logged into the same browser session. If that fails, try clearing cookies or use an incognito window to re-auth. I'll also add you to eng-models which contains model-serving.

devops-bot: Reminder: New-member checklist — accept invite, enable 2FA, add SSH key or PAT, join relevant teams. See https://redwood.internal/onboarding (internal).

samir: Accepted the new invite. Org shows up now but model-serving repo still missing.

charles: That usually means you're not yet added to the team with access. I just added you to eng-models with write permissions on model-serving. Refresh or go directly to https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-serving

samir: I can see the repo now and cloned successfully. SSH key added and push worked. Thanks all! :tada:

marta: Great — @charles can you also check CI permissions if Samir needs to trigger workflows?

charles: Done — gave Samir write on workflows. If you hit Actions secret access errors ping me.

samir: All good, closing out. Appreciate the help :)
